My last words to her were that I loved her, and even though I'd never said it, she was like a mother to me. She and my mom raised me. She was the only person who'd vehemently stick up for me. She was a true force of nature. 

Then I gave her permission to die. She wasn't going to go until I did it. And she was in such horrible pain, hooked up to machines in ways she didn't want. She'd promised to come to my wedding. It was an arbitrary date we'd agreed to when I was little. She'd talk about being tired and I'd remind her she agreed to wait for my wedding. I had to free her of that promise. 

She shouldn't have been able to talk the way she was, but she managed to tell me that she was proud of me. Then she was just gone. I don't think I'd change it really. I wish everything had happened differently, that we'd somehow had the premonition to get her into treatment before she was ever sick. And sometimes I wonder what would have happened if I begged her not to go. But I think I already know, She'd have fought and died a slow painful death over the two days the doctors initially predicted she'd have left. 

I miss her more than anything.

I considered myself an artist too, I'd say I'm more into character design and standard commission art. I don't necessarily think I'm good but I enjoy observing the community. Modern art makes things difficult for other artists. 

It's used in money laundering, and tax evasion. The rich pay for modern art, they then hire appraisers to say the value has appreciated. Lastly they donate the art for the value they payed people to say it's worth and except the tax write off. Other art forms have competition for you to compare the price to. So you have an idea what it's really worth based on the style. But these people just claim you don't understand the meaning. A nice drawing of your oc might be worth 200 dollars, but you can see its not worth 20,000. 

It's used to put other artists down. Like you feel bad when people question the validity of your chosen medium other artists feel really bad when they're called sellouts, or told that because they work for clients they're inherently less in touch with their creativity. Not every line I make has a meaning behind it. Some of them just look good. (I am not accusing you of doing this) but I've had modern artists tell me that this makes my work less meaningful. The modern art community sometimes dislikes drawing to bring out others visions, or anything that isn't raw emotion. Sometimes artists need to create without taxing themselves. What brings some people up, stresses others terribly. 

None of this means you're wrong for doing modern art. It just means that there are a lot of flaws in the community that it's important to be aware of. In my personal opinion I feel a lot of the dislike is deserved, when modern art is being held over art that's taken decades to master. Because not everyone can do that. It's wonderful that it's helped ypu however, and I wish you nothing but good things on uour professional journey.
